chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Imran ibn Musa from Al-Hasan ibn Tariq from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, raising it, said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And prepare against them whatever force you can and horses tied at the frontier': 'Archery'.

key_terms.رِبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ: horses tied at the frontier/military readiness

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'whatever force you can' refer to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this exegetical hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) clarifies that the 'force' mentioned in Surah Al-Anfal (8:60) specifically encompasses archery, reflecting the primary military technology of the early Islamic era. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical martial skills as a tangible manifestation of spiritual and communal strength (*quwwah*) necessary for defense and jihad.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Imran Bin Musa, from Al Hassan Bin Tareyf, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, raising it, said,
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [8:60] And prepare against them whatever force you can and horses tied at the frontier: ‘The archery’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from abu ‘Abd Allah who has narrated the following from his ancestors: “Sharp shooting is an arrow of the arrows of al-Islam.”
